stem: A 6-week-old infant has a harsh pansystolic murmur and a chest radiograph shows cardiomegaly with increased pulmonary vascular markings; which diagnosis is most likely?
explanation: Ventricular septal defect is the most likely diagnosis.

citations.source: Louisa Leone MD3 2025 - Child and Adolescent Health - Study Notes.pdf
citations.title: Louisa Leone MD3 2025 - Child and Adolescent Health - Study Notes.pdf

optionExplanations.A: Incorrect because atrial septal defect typically causes an atrial left-to-right shunt and is not classically associated with a harsh pansystolic murmur.
optionExplanations.B: Incorrect because patent ductus arteriosus usually produces a continuous murmur rather than a harsh pansystolic murmur.
optionExplanations.C: Correct because ventricular septal defect classically presents at 4 to 8 weeks with a harsh pansystolic murmur, cardiomegaly, and increased pulmonary vascular markings.
optionExplanations.D: Incorrect because an innocent murmur is usually a systolic ejection or musical vibratory murmur with a normal examination, not cardiomegaly and pulmonary plethora.
optionExplanations.E: Incorrect because atrioventricular septal defect does not best fit this classic combination of a harsh pansystolic murmur and chest radiograph findings.
